# sherpa-node-lane

One SWIMLANE of a workflow: a row down a [sherpa-layout-canvas](sherpa-layout-canvas.md), in its `rows` slot, the whole width, faint in its colour, its name at the start of what the view shows. A JUNCTION is the band between two lanes where a logic node stands: no fill, a dotted edge. Its host writes where it stands and how tall (data-y, data-h, plane px): it pans and zooms down, never across. It takes no press. Will, 2026-11-10

## When to use it

For the swimlanes of a workflow on a `sherpa-layout-canvas`: one row each, in its `rows` slot, the whole width, its name at the start of what the view shows. Its host writes where it stands and how tall (`data-y`, `data-h`, plane px) and its colour; `data-type="junction"` is the band between two lanes where a logic node stands. It takes no press. For columns across the canvas, use `sherpa-node-stage`.

## Example

```html
<sherpa-layout-canvas style="inline-size: 900px; block-size: 420px"><sherpa-node-lane slot="rows" data-heading="Data" data-y="40" data-h="140"></sherpa-node-lane><sherpa-node-lane slot="rows" data-type="junction" data-heading="Junction" data-y="196" data-h="80"></sherpa-node-lane><sherpa-node-lane slot="rows" data-heading="Agentic" data-colour="#7b3bcd" data-y="292" data-h="120"></sherpa-node-lane><sherpa-node data-heading="Source" data-icon="storage" data-x="120" data-y="80" data-output-socket="object"></sherpa-node></sherpa-layout-canvas>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-colour` | text |  | a CSS colour its band wears; none, the default look |
| `data-h` | number | `0` | its height, in plane px |
| `data-heading` | text | `Lane` | its name (default Lane) |
| `data-type` | `lane` `junction` | `lane` | lane \| junction : a junction has no fill, and a dotted edge |
| `data-y` | number | `0` | its top, in plane px |

## Parts

Style these from outside with `::part()`:

`band`, `heading`, `label`, `swatch`
